Package com.example.cosmos_discovery.database

Class EventService

java.lang.Object
com.example.cosmos_discovery.database.EventService
public class EventService extends Object
Provides event-related Firestore operations. All methods are async. Use Consumer<T> onSuccess for results and Consumer<String> onFailure for error messages — the same pattern as AuthService.

  • Method Details

    • listenThisWeekEvents

      public com.google.firebase.firestore.ListenerRegistration listenThisWeekEvents(Consumer<List<Event>> onUpdate, Consumer<String> onError)
      Attaches a real-time listener for approved events in the current calendar week (Sunday 00:00 → Saturday 23:59:59). onUpdate fires immediately with the current data, then again whenever a document is added, changed, or removed. NOTE: Requires a composite Firestore index on (status ASC, dateTime ASC). On first run, Logcat will print a link — click it to auto-create the index.
      Returns:
      a ListenerRegistration — call .remove() in onStop() to detach and stop streaming updates.

    • listenUpcomingEvents

      public com.google.firebase.firestore.ListenerRegistration listenUpcomingEvents(Consumer<List<Event>> onUpdate, Consumer<String> onError)
      Attaches a real-time listener for all approved events with a future dateTime, ordered chronologically. Use this for a full "upcoming events" feed.
      Returns:
      a ListenerRegistration — call .remove() in onStop()

    • fetchRecentEvents

      public void fetchRecentEvents(int limit, Consumer<List<Event>> onSuccess, Consumer<String> onFailure)
      Fetches the limit most recently created approved events, ordered by createdAt descending. Used for "Suggested" cards.

    • addEvent

      public void addEvent(Event event, Consumer<String> onSuccess, Consumer<String> onFailure)
      Writes a new event document to Firestore. The document ID is auto-generated. onSuccess receives the new document ID so callers can set event.setId().

    • removeEvent

      public void removeEvent(String eventId, Runnable onSuccess, Consumer<String> onFailure)
      Deletes the event document with the given ID.

    • updateEventStatus

      public void updateEventStatus(String eventId, String status, Runnable onSuccess, Consumer<String> onFailure)
      Updates the status field of an event. Use the constants on Event: Event.STATUS_APPROVED, Event.STATUS_PENDING, Event.STATUS_REJECTED.

    • fetchEventById

      public void fetchEventById(String eventId, Consumer<Event> onSuccess, Consumer<String> onFailure)
      Fetches a single event by its document ID. One-shot read.

    • rsvpToEvent

      public void rsvpToEvent(String eventId, String userId, Runnable onSuccess, Consumer<String> onFailure)
      Adds userId to the event's attendeeIds array and increments rsvpCount by 1. Both updates are applied atomically via a single Firestore document update.

    • cancelRsvp

      public void cancelRsvp(String eventId, String userId, Runnable onSuccess, Consumer<String> onFailure)
      Removes userId from the event's attendeeIds array and decrements rsvpCount by 1. Both updates are applied atomically.

    • fetchCategories

      public void fetchCategories(Consumer<List<String>> onSuccess, Consumer<String> onFailure)
      One-shot fetch of all category names from the categories collection. Each document must have a name String field. Results are sorted alphabetically. Used to populate the filter overlay's category chips.
